Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure private listing - revenue recognition & tax exhibit

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for walking us through the private offer flow yesterday. Our procurement and finance teams have a couple of asks before we can approve the listing on Azure Marketplace:

- We need a short revenue recognition exhibit that clarifies the billing cadence and which party recognizes revenue for marketplace sales.
- Our tax team also needs confirmation on whether Microsoft/Azure will withhold VAT/GST for US/EU customers, and if so, whether Redwood will provide a tax certificate to avoid double withholding.

I attached Greenbridge's standard tax form for your intake. Can you share a proposed exhibit or suggested language we can circulate with our legal? We are aiming to complete procurement review this month.

Best,
Aisha Khan
Sr. Procurement Manager
Greenbridge Health

Hi Aisha —

Appreciate the note and the form. Quick status from our side:

- We do have a short exhibit we use for private offers that lays out the billing flow (Azure invoices customer, Microsoft remits to Redwood, Redwood recognizes revenue on receipt net of marketplace fees) — I will attach a draft for your review.
- On withholding: for EU customers, marketplace mechanics differ by country. Typically Azure may collect VAT at point of sale; in some cases there is withholding for certain countries. Redwood can provide the tax paperwork (W-8/W-9 analogs and VAT registration evidence) where applicable, but we need to confirm the exact country list to advise Greenbridge Finance.

Looping in Marissa for the canonical exhibit language and Jonas to confirm the marketplace tax process from the publisher ops side. If you can share a short list of the countries you sell into, we can be definitive.

Next steps: I will circulate the exhibit draft and an annotated note on withholding. Can we target EOD Wed for that?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman

Hi all —

Thanks Aisha — attaching our suggested exhibit language (proposed_revrec_exhibit_v1.docx). High-level notes:

1) Revenue recognition: we propose the following sentence be included in the private offer terms: "For marketplace sales processed via Microsoft Azure Marketplace, Microsoft invoices the Customer and remits Net Proceeds to Redwood Inference. Redwood Inference recognizes revenue upon remittance of Net Proceeds, net of marketplace fees and any applicable taxes."

2) Tax withholding: we suggest a clause that commits Redwood to provide valid tax documentation within 10 business days upon request to support refund/credit claims if withholding is applied by a marketplace or tax authority. However, Redwood cannot guarantee refund outcomes — those depend on local tax authorities/publishing platform practices.

3) We should include a short section that defines what constitutes "Net Proceeds" and references marketplace fee schedules.

Ben — can you have Tax/Finance confirm whether Redwood will or can issue a standardized tax certificate for EU VAT reversal claims? Jonas — please confirm whether Azure withholds for any US states or typical EU VAT flows we should call out.

Marissa Cole
Head of Marketplaces Partnerships
Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_revrec_exhibit_v1.docx
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@greenbridgehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private listing - revenue recognition & tax exhibit

Thanks — I reviewed the exhibit and ran it by our legal. They have a few redlines around the tax language (they want a tighter commitment on documentation timing and a mechanism if withholding impacts our rev rec). See attached PDF with comments (GB_redlines_revrec.pdf).

Key asks from Greenbridge legal:
- If withholding occurs and Red provides documentation supporting a refund, include a timeline for Redwood to assist in the refund process and escalate to publisher ops if needed.
- Define a compensation path if withholding leads to quantifiable lost margin for Greenbridge on the first 90 days post-listing (they are open to a one-time credit if material).

If Redwood is comfortable with a limited credit cap and an escalation path, we can move to DocuSign next week. Otherwise, they will require additional legal review.

Best,
Aisha
Attachment: GB_redlines_revrec.pdf
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@greenbridgehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private listing - revenue recognition & tax exhibit

Aisha —

Thanks for the redlines and clear asks. Summary of Redwood's proposed positions: 

- Documentation: Redwood will provide tax and remittance evidence within 7 business days of a documented withholding event and will actively engage publisher ops to assist Greenbridge in pursuing a refund or credit.
- Escalation: Redwood will escalate to Microsoft rep and provide reasonable supporting materials; we cannot compel Microsoft outcomes, but we will own the escalation on behalf of the partner.
- One-time credit: Redwood is willing to provide a one-time, capped credit equal to the documented withholding amount up to a cap of $10,000 for the first 90 days post-listing, provided Greenbridge supplies evidence of actual margin impact.

Please confirm whether that structure would be acceptable to Greenbridge legal. If so, Marissa and I will prepare a clean exhibit and a short amendment sheet and route for DocuSign. Target: sign by Tue, 29 Jul.

Next steps for Redwood internal: Ben, please confirm tax can issue the paperwork and the $10k cap is acceptable from an accounting/risk perspective. Jonas, please prepare a brief note on typical Azure withholding mechanics to attach to the exhibit.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
